channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: NASCAR Is Targeting the Young Fans, CEO Says
item.description: Steve O'Donnell, NASCAR CEO, says the business has good momentum but he's still focused on attracting younger viewers and getting new fans to the track. He also talks about competition among the drivers and how that helps the sport. He speaks on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Millennium Nears $100 Billion as Giant Hedge Funds Enter New Era
item.description: Millennium Management's assets have hit $97 billion, more than double what the firm oversaw six years ago, and is speeding toward $100 billion. Hema Parmar reports on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Firms Seek to Lower Borrowing Costs in Flurry of US Repricings
item.description: Companies are flocking to the US leveraged loan market with offerings to reprice large chunks of existing debt, tapping strong investor demand to reduce borrowing costs.
item.dc:creator: Jeannine Amodeo

item.title: Luxury Whiskey Bets on Ready-Made Cocktails
item.description: Julie Macklowe, the Founder of the luxury whiskey brand Macklowe, joined Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about how tariffs on liquor ultimately punish American consumers through higher prices, and may even be contributing to younger generations drinking less. She also explains why convenience is driving her latest bet: a premium, ready-to-serve whiskey cocktail designed to make the traditionally "snobby" category more accessible. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Saudi Arabia Halts Energy Sites as Houthis Claim New Attacks
item.description:
Saudi Arabia halted several energy facilities in the south, as the Iran-backed Houthi militants claimed fresh strikes on the kingdom. The Yemen-based Houthis said they targeted Saudi Aramco’s facilities in Abha, Najran and Jazan with ballistic missiles and drones, the group’s military spokesperson said in a statement. The attacks caused fires at several locations, and efforts were ongoing to contain the blazes, the Saudi energy ministry said on X, without naming the facilities.
While the targets appear to include infrastructure that supply the local Saudi demand, repeated attacks on Jazan, where a major refinery is located, are a concern for the oil market. For the latest, we speak with Becca Wasser, Defense Lead for Bloomberg Economics. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Carney Says Tariffs on US Goods Meant to Protect Canada, Not Escalate Conflict
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney said he doesn’t believe in escalating the trade war with the US, but he argued counter-tariffs are necessary to cushion the blow for Canadian businesses and workers.
item.dc:creator: Nojoud Al Mallees

item.title: India’s Strong Growth Gives Confidence to World, Modi Says
item.description: Speaking after inaugurating the Global Fintech Fest, India's prime minister Narendra Modi said the country's reforms express will continue. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Odd Lots: Why Money Launderers Love $100 Bills
item.description: On this episode of the Odd Lots podcast, journalist Oliver Bullough joins Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal to discuss why criminal enterprises love to launder money in the form of $100 bills and why money laundering resembles Renaissance-era banking. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Targets Iran’s Airlines As New Sanctions Push Continues
item.description: The US took action against dozens of firms supporting Iran’s aviation sector on Tuesday, as part of a new sanctions effort from the Trump administration that hasn’t yet appeared to have much impact on Tehran’s main trading partners.
item.dc:creator: Yash Roy

item.title: Private Credit’s Tokenization Revolution
item.description: Apex Group CEO Peter Hughes joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why family offices need better access to quality private-market deals. He also makes the case that regulated tokenization could transform private credit, bringing 24/7 access, secondary-market liquidity and a potential end to traditional seven-to-10-year lockups. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Odd Lots: How Is Farm Equipment Used for Money Laundering?
item.description: On this episode of the Odd Lots podcast, journalist Oliver Bullough joins Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal to discuss how Mexican cartels use heavy farm equipment to launder money and why criminals are always looking for creative ways to move cash. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China Ships Out First Sulfuric Acid Cargo Since Halt on Exports
item.description: China has allowed its first outbound shipment of sulfuric acid since May, offering some relief to copper producers squeezed by a global shortage after the Iran war choked off Middle East supplies.
item.dc:creator: Julian Luk

item.title: Novartis and Boston Scientific Slide, Intel Price Hikes | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Novartis (NOVN) shares are lower as it suffered its third clinical-trial setback in a week after a treatment for a rare muscle-wasting disease failed a late-stage study.
- Boston Scientific (BSX) shares are moving on news it said that fallout from a cybersecurity incident has impacted its ability to ship its products to customers and will cause the medical devices company to miss its sales growth and earnings estimates for the year.
- Intel (INTC) is rising on a report that the company could raise computer chip prices next month. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Volatility Limits Post-Labor Day US Bond Rush to Six-Year Low
item.description: The US investment-grade debt market is having its quietest post-Labor Day rush in six years, as fresh market volatility is keeping some borrowers on the sidelines.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Kingsbury

item.title: Senegal to Negotiate Debt Reprofiling in Creditor Talks
item.description: Senegal will seek to negotiate a debt reprofiling instead of a restructuring in talks with creditors, as the West African nation moves to make its loans sustainable to qualify for an International Monetary Fund program.
item.dc:creator: Katarina Höije and Moses Mozart Dzawu

item.title: Buyout Debt Worth $138 Billion Set to Land in Credit Markets
item.description: Credit investors look set to be spoiled for choice as bankers gear up to offload in excess of $138 billion of buyout debt in coming months.
item.dc:creator: Claire Ruckin and Eleanor Duncan

item.title: Saudi Arabia Halts Energy Sites as Houthis Claim New Attacks
item.description: Saudi Arabia halted several energy facilities in the south, as the Iran-backed Houthi militants claimed fresh strikes on the kingdom.
item.dc:creator: Rakteem Katakey and Ahmed Elimam

item.title: Gold Wavers as Traders Weigh Mideast Tensions and Dollar Moves
item.description: Gold wavered, as traders weighed the competing effects of rising Middle East tensions and the US dollar’s decline against the yen.
item.dc:creator: Preeti Soni

item.title: Stocks Fall as Oil Gain Stokes Inflation Worries: Markets Wrap
item.description: An advance in oil prices sent stocks lower, fueling concerns about higher interest rates just days ahead of key inflation data.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Heineken Highlights Nonalcoholic Beer, Serena Williams in US Open Partnership
item.description:
Maggie Timoney, CEO of Heineken USA, said Heineken's 0.0 nonalcoholic beer has seen success because consumers are looking to moderate their alcohol consumption, even if they're not looking to cut it out entirely. Timoney said that the beverage company wanted to honor the history of the US Open and the six championships won by Serena Williams in their partnership with the tennis star.
Correct: An earlier version of this post, misspelled Heineken (Source: Bloomberg)
